title: 2004 Hendrick Motorsports aircraft crash
summary: A Beechcraft King Air conducting an instrument approach in low-level overcast at Blue Ridge Airport failed to properly descend through the approach procedure. The aircraft overflew the airport by 4 nautical miles before reaching the minimum descent altitude of 1400 feet, then initiated a missed approach. The aircraft crashed into Bull Mountain during the attempted climb-out, killing all ten occupants.
probable_cause: The pilots failed to execute the instrument approach procedure and failed to use all navigational aids to confirm the airplane's position during approach. The aircraft overflew the airport by 4 nautical miles before reaching the minimum descent altitude, then initiated a missed approach that resulted in controlled flight into terrain (p. 6)

factors.evidence: Aircraft failed to descend to assigned 2600-foot altitude immediately upon ATC clearance for approach; did not begin descending until 4nm past BALES LOM (p. 2)
Pilots failed to use all navigational aids including GPS with current database to confirm position; GPS database not current for IFR use (p. 3)
Instrument meteorological conditions prevailed with 400-600 foot ceiling and 1.25-5 mile visibility; state trooper stated visibility 0-0.25 mile at mountain (p. 4)
Aircraft reached MDA of 1400 feet only after overflying airport by 4 nautical miles; flew level at 1400-1500 feet for 1:13 before initiating climb (p. 2-3)
Aircraft crashed into Bull Mountain peak during missed approach climb - initial impact in trees with wreckage found at elevation 2450 feet (p. 3, 5)

events.text: Beechcraft King Air 200 N501RH departed Concord Regional Airport (p. 1)
Flight established in holding pattern over BALES LOM at 4000 feet, second in line for runway 30 approach (p. 1)
ATC cleared airplane for localizer runway 30 approach (p. 2)
Flight crew advised controller airplane was established inbound on approach (p. 2)
Controller cleared airplane for approach and approved frequency change to CTAF (p. 2)
Airplane began descent from 4000 feet at 4 DME (2nm after BALES LOM) (p. 2)
Airplane leveled off at 1400-1500 feet about 4nm beyond MTV and 5nm beyond the MAP - significantly overflew airport (p. 2)
Flight crew declared missed approach to controller (p. 2)
MSAW alert sounded on controller radar at 1230:07 when airplane at 1800 feet, 2.5nm NW of airport - controller did not observe alert (p. 5)
Radar target lost at 1233:24 as airplane crashed into Bull Mountain in Stuart, Virginia at elevation 2400 feet (p. 3)

notes: NTSB Aircraft Accident Brief read (24 pages)
Detailed radar data and flight path analysis provided
